on_complete.text: The jackdaw in the castle courtyard hatched four eggs that week, and Lady Agathe named every one.
Dumpling played the tail again the next year, and the year after, and hummed through every one.
The six buoys went back to the lighthouse and sat on Sanna's windowsill, looking pleased.
The net-menders on the quay sing the Founder's song now while they work. Most of them think it was always a song.
Fenna's chorus sang the sea crossing in four parts, one of them from inside a barrel.
Fenna sang the sea crossing on her own, and very well, and told everyone afterwards where her chorus had been.
Elin's curtain hung three paces back from the stage, and the fire lane stayed clear. Vidar Foss was seen clapping.
The old curtain did its best, and Elin's new one stayed folded on her loom for next year.
The whole square shouts for it again. Lady Agathe says she will come down every year until she is a hundred, and Hedda writes it down.
The town goes home pleased, full of loaf, arguing gently about who sang loudest.
Nobody can agree how the legend ends. Does the Dragon eat the loaf? Did it ever? The town argues happily on the square until the stars come out, and all the next year.
